title: Flexbox vs Grid
description: Understand when to use Flexbox vs CSS Grid for layouts.

options.text: Flexbox is one-dimensional (row OR column) while Grid is two-dimensional (rows AND columns)
options.explanation: Flexbox lays items out along a single axis (main axis). Grid works in both dimensions simultaneously. Use Flexbox for navigation bars, card rows; Grid for full page layouts, image galleries.

options.text: CSS Grid cannot create responsive layouts without media queries
options.explanation: Grid has built-in responsive features: `auto-fill`/`auto-fit` with `minmax()` creates responsive grids without media queries. E.g., `grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(250px, 1fr))`.

options.text: Flexbox items cannot wrap to multiple lines
options.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap allows flex items to wrap onto multiple lines. Combined with flex-basis, this creates responsive card layouts without media queries.

options.text: You should never use Flexbox and Grid together
options.explanation: They complement each other perfectly. A common pattern: Grid for the overall page layout, Flexbox for component-level alignment within grid cells.
